---
title: "Named Entity Recognition (NER)"
description: "A natural language processing task that identifies and labels mentions of entities such as people, organizations, and places."
term: "Named Entity Recognition (NER)"
letter: "N"
category: "NLP"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Named entity recognition finds meaningful names and quantities in text and
labels their types. In "Ada works at Acme in London," a NER system might
identify Ada as a person, Acme as an organization, and London as a location.

## Technical explanation

NER is commonly framed as sequence labeling: a model assigns a tag to each
token or token span. Schemes such as BIO mark the beginning and inside of an
entity span, while modern systems may predict spans directly. Entity
categories are defined by the dataset or application.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

NER can turn unstructured text into structured fields for document search,
analytics, knowledge graphs, and workflow automation. Entity labels and
quality requirements are domain-specific, so production systems need
evaluation on representative data and careful handling of sensitive
entities.

## How it works

Text is tokenized and passed to a model that uses the surrounding context
to predict token labels or entity spans. A post-processing step may merge
subword tokens and enforce valid span boundaries. Performance is often
measured with precision, recall, and F1 at the entity-span level.

## Practical example

A support-ticket pipeline could detect product names, dates, and order
identifiers, then make tickets easier to route or search. Since a missed
identifier can affect downstream work, the system should be tested on
realistic ticket formats before automation.

## Common misconceptions

- NER identifies entity mentions; it does not necessarily resolve which real-world entity a mention refers to.
- A model's entity categories are not universal and may not match a new domain.
- Correctly tagging a word does not establish that the extracted information is true.
